To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a supervised machine learning approach is a viable alternative to the standard unsupervised ones for link prediction in coauthoring networks; (2) the use of the dual graph can significantly boost the performance of supervised link prediction in co-authors networks; (3) the best results are obtained when the dual graph is combined with the co-authoring graph in a single model.

a) a topological dyad based supervised machine learning approach to link prediction can be successfully applied to co-authoring networks; and b) link prediction performances can benefit from the analysis of both co-authoring and dual graphs.

(i) the dual graph is an interesting graph for academic collaboration prediction; (ii) the dual graph can be exploited for link prediction in the co-authoring graph; (iii) the supervised machine learning approach is more effective than a simple topological approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: given an authoring graph, how do we predict the future co-authorship relations among authors?
the problem of recommending new co-authoring links in a scientific collaboration network, based on information contained in both the co-authoring and the dual graphs.
the following question: can the link prediction task be enhanced by using the dual graph?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach, by exploiting both the original and dual graphs, is able to outperform the best state-of-the-art methods for co-authoring networks link prediction.
a supervised machine learning link-prediction approach can be successfully applied to the co-authoring networks, provided that the dual network is taken into account as well.
the proposed approach can be used to recommend new collaborations for a researcher based on his/her past collaborations and publications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new supervised machine learning approach that outperforms state-of-the-art approaches for link prediction on co-authoring networks.
we have shown that the dual graph can be exploited in order to improve link prediction performances.
we show that the use of a supervised machine learning link recommendation approach is very effective in academic collaboration recommendation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the link prediction problem in co-authoring networks can benefit from the analysis of the dual graph, which can be seen as a co-publication network.
link prediction in coauthorship networks can be significantly enhanced by considering both the coauthoring and the dual graph.
the dual graph can provide a complementary information to the co-authoring graph, thus improving the link prediction performances.
